title: What Happens If Your Hiccups Won't Stop?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Hiccups' (hiccups are repeated spasms of your diaphragm paired with a 'hic' sound from your vocal cords closing; the glottis suddenly closes to stop more air from coming in; persistent hiccups last longer than 48 hours, up to one month; intractable = longer than one month; call your healthcare provider if hiccups last longer than two days; 'Experts haven't found a hiccup cure'): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/17672-hiccups

Cleveland Clinic, 'Diaphragm' (thin, dome-shaped muscle that sits below your lungs and heart; tightens and drops to draw air into the lungs): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21578-diaphragm
NHS, 'Hiccups' (hiccups should only last a few minutes; see a GP if they last more than 48 hours; there's no evidence home remedies work for everyone): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hiccups/

Guinness World Records, 'Longest attack of hiccups' (Charles Osborne, USA, 1894-1991, started hiccoughing in 1922 while attempting to weigh a hog before slaughtering it, continued until a morning in February 1990; never found a cure; had two wives and eight children): https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/67619-longest-attack-of-hiccups

Smithsonian Magazine, Kellie Gormly, 'The Curious Case of Charles Osborne, Who Hiccuped for 68 Years Straight', 2022-06-13 (hiccups began after a June 13, 1922 accident while hanging a hog near Union, Nebraska: 'I picked it up and then I fell down'; 20 to 40 involuntary diaphragm spasms per minute; an estimated 430 million hiccups; 'For reasons unknown, Osborne's hiccups suddenly stopped in 1990'; doctors never found a cure or confirmed cause; married twice and had eight children; died May 1991 at 97): https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/the-curious-case-of-charles-osborne-who-hiccuped-for-68-years-straight-180980232/

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Brain Freeze' (scientific term: sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia; brief, intense pain in the front of the head; usually lasts a few seconds to two minutes; press your tongue or thumb against the roof of your mouth to transfer warmth): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21478-brain-freeze

lines.text: What happens if your hiccups won't stop?
One man hiccuped for sixty-eight years straight.
So where does the hic even come from?
Your diaphragm, the muscle under your lungs, suddenly spasms,
air rushes in, and your vocal cords snap shut. Hic!
lines.caps: AIR *RUSHES IN | AND YOUR *VOCAL | CORDS *SNAP | SHUT. *HIC!

lines.text: but past two days, doctors call them persistent.
In nineteen twenty-two, Charles Osborne picked up a hog,
fell, and started hiccuping, twenty to forty times a minute.
Still, he married twice and had eight kids.
Then in nineteen ninety, they just stopped. Nobody knows why.
lines.caps: THEN IN *1990 | THEY JUST *STOPPED | NOBODY KNOWS *WHY

lines.text: Yours hit two days? See a doctor. Don't wait sixty-eight years.
